definition: belonging to or in the possession of a particular person, company, or government

collocations.example: The clinic is privately owned and well funded.
The airport is still state owned.

definition: to put things into a bag, box, or case, especially for traveling or storage

collocations.example: Let's pack up our things and leave now.
We packed all the files into one box.

definition: one side of a sheet of paper in a book, magazine, or document

collocations.example: The story appeared on the front page.
Please write the page number at the top.

definition: the unpleasant feeling you have when part of your body hurts

collocations.example: She takes medicine for her chronic back pain.
He was clearly in pain after the fall.

definition: a colored liquid that you put on a surface to color or protect it

collocations.example: The walls need a fresh coat of paint.
A sign warned us about the wet paint.

definition: two things of the same type that are used together

collocations.example: She bought a new pair of shoes yesterday.
He needs a pair of glasses for reading.

definition: thin material made in sheets, used for writing or printing on

collocations.example: She wrote the address on a piece of paper.
Please put all your ideas down on paper.

definition: to forgive someone, often used politely when apologizing or asking for something

collocations.example: Pardon me for arriving late to the meeting.
Pardon my asking, but where do you work?

definition: a person's father or mother

collocations.example: As a single parent, she works two jobs.
He was a proud parent at the ceremony.

definition: a public area of land with grass and trees, used for recreation

collocations.example: We hiked all day in the national park.
The children loved the rides at the theme park.

definition: one of the pieces or sections that something is divided into

collocations.example: This task is part of my daily routine.
Travel is a major part of his job.

definition: used to show that you mean one specific thing and not others

collocations.example: He enjoys sports, and tennis in particular.
In this particular case, we made an exception.

definition: a social event where people meet to enjoy themselves

collocations.example: We threw a birthday party for our colleague.
They hosted a dinner party for close friends.

definition: to move past or go from one side of something to the other

collocations.example: We will pass through several towns on the way.
I pass by your office every morning.

definition: the time before the present, and the things that happened then

collocations.example: She worked at this company in the past.
He tends to live in the past too much.

definition: to give someone money for goods, services, or work

collocations.example: I will pay for lunch today.
He promised to pay back the loan soon.

definition: a coin of low value; a very small amount of money

collocations.example: The trip did not cost me a penny.
The holiday was worth every penny we spent.

definition: human beings in general, or a group of them

collocations.example: Many young people struggle to find stable jobs.
Many people attended the annual company meeting.

definition: having no faults or mistakes; as good as it can be

collocations.example: This quiet room is perfect for studying.
The used car is in perfect condition.

definition: used to say that something may be true or may happen, but you are not sure

collocations.example: 'Is it going to rain?' 'Perhaps so.'
Perhaps not everyone agrees with this plan.

definition: a single human being

collocations.example: You must sign the form in person.
Every young person deserves a fair chance.

definition: a picture made using a camera

collocations.example: Let me take a photograph of the team.
The report included an aerial photograph of the site.

definition: to choose someone or something from a group

collocations.example: Please pick out the best candidate for the role.
Customers can pick and choose from many options.

definition: a painting, drawing, or photograph of someone or something

collocations.example: Could you take a picture of us here?
She put the photo in a wooden picture frame.

definition: a part or portion of something that has been separated from the whole

collocations.example: She gave me a piece of chocolate.
He cut off a large piece of bread.

definition: a particular position, point, or area

collocations.example: I looked for a quiet place to read.
Make sure the keys are in the right place.

definition: a set of decisions about how to do something in the future

collocations.example: They presented a detailed business plan to investors.
The team agreed on a clear action plan.

definition: a living thing that grows in soil and usually has leaves and roots

collocations.example: Sunlight is essential for healthy plant growth.
She bought a flowering plant for her desk.

definition: to take part in a game or sport

collocations.example: The boys play football after school every day.
We play basketball at the gym on weekends.

definition: used to make a request or an order more polite

collocations.example: Please note the office closes early today.
Please wait here until your name is called.

definition: a large amount that is enough or more than enough

collocations.example: There is plenty of work to finish today.
We had food and drink in plenty.

definition: used to show that one number or amount is added to another

collocations.example: Two hundred dollars plus tax is the total.
The result may vary plus or minus five percent.

definition: a particular idea, fact, or opinion that is expressed

collocations.example: Please explain the problem from your point of view.
Let me summarize the main point of the report.

definition: the official organization whose job is to keep order and catch criminals

collocations.example: She reported the theft at the police station.
A police officer directed traffic at the junction.

definition: having very little money or few possessions

collocations.example: The charity provides free food for poor people.
She grew up in a very poor family.

definition: modern popular music with a strong beat, liked by many people

collocations.example: She listens to pop music while working.
The pop star released a new album.

definition: the place where someone or something is

collocations.example: Make sure the ladder is firmly in position.
The map shows our current position clearly.

definition: able to be done or to happen

collocations.example: Please reply by Friday if possible.
We will fix the issue as quickly as possible.

definition: the system of sending and delivering letters and parcels

collocations.example: I need to mail this at the post office.
The documents will be sent by post.

definition: a deep round container used for cooking

collocations.example: She stirred the soup in a large cooking pot.
He filled the coffee pot with fresh water.

definition: the basic unit of money in the United Kingdom

collocations.example: The price is listed in pound sterling.
He paid with a ten pound note.

definition: energy, especially electricity, used to make machines work

collocations.example: A backup power supply keeps the servers running.
The new power station supplies the whole city.

definition: to make something or someone ready for a future event or use

collocations.example: We must prepare for the client meeting.
She will prepare material for the training session.

definition: the period of time that is happening now

collocations.example: We have no vacancies at present.
This old custom survives to the present day.

definition: formally gave or showed something to someone

collocations.example: The award was presented by the company director.
She was presented with a certificate of achievement.

definition: newspapers, magazines, and the journalists who work for them

collocations.example: The company held a press conference this morning.
They issued a press release about the merger.

definition: to a fairly large degree; quite but not extremely

collocations.example: The results of the survey were pretty good.
I am pretty sure the shop opens at nine.

definition: the amount of money you must pay to buy something

collocations.example: The market price of oil rose sharply.
They sell quality furniture at a reasonable price.

definition: a male member of a royal family, especially the son of a king or queen

collocations.example: The crown prince will visit the city tomorrow.
The young prince greeted the visiting guests warmly.

definition: a building where criminals are kept as punishment

collocations.example: He spent three years in prison.
The judge gave him a long prison sentence.

definition: used to say that something is very likely to be true or to happen

collocations.example: The flight will most probably be delayed.
He is probably not coming to the meeting.

definition: a situation that is difficult to deal with and needs a solution

collocations.example: The team faced a difficult problem with the software.
A technical problem delayed the morning flight.

definition: a planned series of activities with a particular aim

collocations.example: New staff must complete the training program.
The city will launch a recycling program next month.

definition: a statement that you will certainly do or not do something

collocations.example: He made a promise to finish the report.
She always keeps a promise to her clients.

definition: right, suitable, or correct for a particular situation

collocations.example: Please file these documents in the proper way.
Everything must be done at the proper time.

definition: to keep someone or something safe from harm or damage

collocations.example: New laws aim to protect the environment better.
A helmet protects you from serious injury.

definition: relating to or available to all the ordinary people in a society

collocations.example: Many commuters rely on public transport daily.
The library is a valuable public service.

definition: to hold something firmly and use force to move it toward yourself

collocations.example: She pulled on the rope to ring the bell.
The child pulled at his mother's sleeve.

definition: to press against something in order to move it away from you

collocations.example: He pushed against the heavy door with both hands.
Push down firmly on the lid to close it.

definition: to move something into a particular place or position

collocations.example: She put down her bag on the chair.
Please put away the files after the meeting.

definition: a period of three months, used especially for business accounts

collocations.example: Sales rose during the first quarter of the year.
The company expects growth in the fourth quarter.

definition: a female ruler of a country, or the wife of a king

collocations.example: She was crowned queen of the small nation.
The reigning queen opened the new hospital today.

definition: a sentence or phrase that asks for information

collocations.example: He could not answer the question correctly.
Feel free to ask a question after the talk.

definition: done or happening in a short time; fast

collocations.example: We appreciate your quick response to our email.
The restaurant is known for its quick service.

definition: making very little or no noise

collocations.example: Please keep quiet during the presentation.
We enjoyed a quiet night at home.

definition: to a fairly large degree; rather

collocations.example: Her spoken English is quite good now.
The meeting went quite well today.

definition: a small animal with long ears and soft fur that lives in holes in the ground

collocations.example: A wild rabbit darted across the open field.
Their pet rabbit lives in a wooden hutch.

definition: a competition to see who or what is the fastest

collocations.example: They placed a bet on the horse race.
Our team won the relay race quite easily.

definition: the activity of broadcasting sound, or a device for receiving it

collocations.example: I heard the news on the radio.
She works at a local radio station.

definition: water that falls from the clouds in drops

collocations.example: The match was canceled due to heavy rain.
They waited for the bus in the rain.

definition: to increase an amount, level, or standard

collocations.example: Suppliers decided to raise the price of materials.
The new policy aims to raise standards everywhere.

definition: a fixed amount or proportion, often measured against something else

collocations.example: The bank lowered the interest rate again.
The exchange rate changed in our favor.

definition: used to show that you prefer one thing or option to another

collocations.example: I would rather stay home tonight.
She walked to work rather than drove.

definition: to succeed in achieving something, such as a decision, after effort

collocations.example: The two sides finally reached an agreement.
The committee could not reach a conclusion.

definition: to look at and understand the meaning of written words

collocations.example: She likes to read a book before bed.
The teacher asked him to read aloud.

definition: prepared and able to do something or to be used

collocations.example: Give me five minutes to get ready.
Are you ready for the interview tomorrow?

definition: actually existing or true; not imagined or false

collocations.example: The film is based on real life events.
This bag is cheap, but mine is the real thing.

definition: to understand or become aware of something clearly

collocations.example: Over time she came to realise her mistake.
I did not fully realise how hard it was.

definition: used to emphasize something, meaning very or very much

collocations.example: The food at the new restaurant was really good.
I really like working with this team.

definition: a cause or explanation for something that happens

collocations.example: What is the reason for the delay?
The main reason for leaving was low pay.

definition: happening or done a short time ago

collocations.example: In recent years, demand has grown steadily.
The report covers every recent development in the field.

definition: a written account of facts kept for future reference

collocations.example: The nurse updated the patient's medical record.
The office keeps a record of every visitor.

definition: having the color of blood or fire

collocations.example: He ordered a glass of red wine.
Her face turned bright red with embarrassment.

definition: to understand or feel a connection with someone or something

collocations.example: Many customers relate to our brand story.
Good managers relate well to their staff.

definition: to keep something in your mind or bring it back to your mind

collocations.example: Please remember to lock the office door.
I do not remember signing that contract.

definition: money that you pay regularly to use a room, house, or property

collocations.example: They struggle to pay the rent each month.
The monthly rent includes water and electricity.

definition: something that you say or write as an answer

collocations.example: She nodded in reply to his question.
I sent an email but got no reply.

definition: a written or spoken account giving information about something

collocations.example: Shareholders received the company's annual report today.
A news report described the storm damage.

definition: having the job or duty to deal with or take care of something

collocations.example: She is responsible for training new employees.

definition: a period of time when you relax or sleep to regain energy

collocations.example: Let's have a rest after this long walk.
You need a good rest before the exam.

definition: was supported on or leaning against something

collocations.example: His elbows rested on the wooden table.
The ladder rested against the brick wall.

definition: to come back to a place or go back to it

collocations.example: He will return home after the conference ends.
She plans to return to work next month.

definition: having a lot of money or valuable possessions

collocations.example: He hopes to get rich through careful investing.
She comes from a very rich family.

definition: to remove or free yourself from something unwanted

collocations.example: We need to get rid of these old files.
He could not rid himself of the doubt.

definition: to sit on and control a bicycle, motorcycle, or animal as it moves

collocations.example: She learned to ride a bike at five.
They taught the children to ride a horse.

definition: correct, true, or suitable for a situation

collocations.example: Yes, that's right, the meeting is at noon.
You called me at just the right time.

definition: things that you are morally or legally allowed to have or do

collocations.example: Workers should know their legal rights well.
The group campaigns for human rights worldwide.

definition: a piece of jewelry worn on the finger

collocations.example: She wore a simple gold wedding ring.
He gave her a beautiful diamond ring.

definition: to increase in amount, number, or level

collocations.example: The property will rise in value over time.
Interest rates could rise again next month.

definition: a large natural stream of water that flows into the sea

collocations.example: They had a picnic on the river bank.
A new bridge lets cars cross the river.
